fatten() method for fiber::bundle_set objects

Source: R/fatten.R
fatten-fiber-bundle_set-method.Rd

Fatens every fiber::bundle in a fiber::bundle_set independently, each with its own visibility floor and pruning decision, and returns a set of the resulting bundles. See fatten() for the full parameter documentation.

Arguments

x

A fiber::streamline, fiber::bundle, or fiber::bundle_set.

visibility

Numeric. The smallest tube radius considered visible to the naked eye. NULL (default) derives it from the streamlines' sampling density (the median intra-streamline step); a positive number overrides the floor.

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

A fiber::bundle_set in which every streamline carries a per-streamline radius; dense bundles hold their pruned subset, and bundles pruned down to zero streamlines are dropped.

See also

fatten()

Examples

library(fiber)

# Two bundles of line-only streamlines in one set: a sparse fanning tract and
# a densely packed one. Each is fattened independently.
fan <- function(i) {
  t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 200)
  fiber::streamline(cbind(
    X = seq_len(200) * 0.1,
    Y = 0.25 * sin(t) + (i - 3.5) * 1.5,
    Z = 0.25 * cos(t)
  ))
}
pack <- function(i) {
  t <- seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 100)
  fiber::streamline(cbind(
    X = seq_len(100) * 0.5,
    Y = 0.5 + (i - 3.5) * 0.3,
    Z = 0.25 * sin(t) + (i - 3.5) * 0.05
  ))
}
cs <- fiber::bundle_set(list(
  fan  = fiber::bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), fan)),
  pack = fiber::bundle(lapply(seq_len(6), pack))
))

fattened <- fatten(cs)
vapply(fattened@bundles, function(b) length(b@streamlines), integer(1L))
#> [1] 6 2
plot3d(fattened)              # draws real 3D tubes per bundle
#> ℹ Rendering 8 streamlines across 2 bundles...
